solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bureaucrat gives an area around standard one thousand pounds

parts.note: an gives the single letter A

indicators.note: around tells us the word for area wraps itself about the word for standard

parts.note: a patch is a small area of ground
par is the standard or norm, as in 'up to par'
I is the Roman numeral for one
K (kilo) is slang for a thousand, especially a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A civil servant pays out a generous sum on top of some benchmark figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' is only a link; 'around' wraps the area word about the standard word. 'one thousand pounds' looks like a single sum but gives two pieces: Roman one and K for a grand.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparatchik is a party functionary in the Soviet system, hence any rigid official or bureaucrat.

clue.text: North African boy with some study of age at heart

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
something placed at the heart of a word sits in its middle, so the boy's name is opened up

parts.note: Alan is a boy's name

indicators.note: some means only part of the word is used, here its first four letters

parts.note: geriatrics is the medical study of old age

explanation.surface: A lad from North Africa has an interest in ageing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' keeps only the first part of the study word, and 'with ... at heart' sets that inside the boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a country of North Africa, so a native of it is a North African.

clue.text: Places to set out for carnivores

indicators.note: set out suggests arranging items afresh, so the letters of the first two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somewhere to arrange meat-eaters, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' belongs to the indicator, not the fodder: PLACES TO has the right eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Polecats are small meat-eating mammals of the weasel family.

clue.text: Bad guy to rake around piece of garden

indicators.note: around puts the libertine's word about the garden letter

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a roue

indicators.note: a piece of the word garden is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A villain goes out to rake some flowerbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' looks like a garden tool given the garden, but it is a libertine (ROUE), with G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or unprincipled man, a scoundrel.

clue.text: Businessmen on the queen's square?

parts.note: trad, short for traditional, means old-fashioned or square
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; with the possessive it gives ERS

explanation.surface: Merchants stand on the royal plaza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like a town square; here it means conventional, TRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Traders are people who buy and sell goods, businesspeople.

clue.text: Unexciting little sound by musical instrument

parts.note: a hum is a low, faint sound
a drum is a percussion instrument

explanation.surface: A faint noise beside a drum is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Humdrum means dull, monotonous and lacking excitement.

clue.text: Provocative hair licks USSR into shape

indicators.note: putting the letters into shape means reforming them in a new order

explanation.surface: A flirty lock of hair moulds the Soviet Union, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: USSR seems to belong to the communist theme, but it is just fodder with LICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss curl is a small curl of hair pressed flat on the forehead or cheek, often seen as coquettish.

clue.text: RS of the racing world backs crime

indicators.note: backs here means the word for crime is read from back to front

parts.note: murder is the gravest crime

explanation.surface: A champion of the turf turns out to have a criminal past.
explanation.walkthrough: RS stands throughout for 'red star'; the famous racehorse was Red Rum, triple Grand National winner (the Grand National is Britain's great steeplechase).
explanation.definitionFit: Red Rum, three-time Grand National winner, was literally a red star of horse racing.

clue.text: Artist is at home with fruit

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A painter stays in with some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Books in transaction concerned with choppers

indicators.note: in places the books abbreviation inside the word for a transaction

parts.note: a deal is a business transaction
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Ledgers kept for a business deal about axes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental means relating to teeth, which are informally called choppers.

clue.text: Good turn getting convict out of this penal system

parts.note: a U-turn, so U stands for turn
a lag is a convict, as in 'old lag'

explanation.surface: Doing someone a kindness gets a prisoner released from the camps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulag was the Soviet network of forced-labour camps, a penal system.

clue.text: Acknowledgement of being given entry

definitions.meaning: confession of a fact or a fault
the act of being let in

explanation.definitionFit: Admission means both a confession of something and the granting of entrance.

clue.text: Criminal tennis player?

definitions.meaning: playfully, one who wields a racket

explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a fraudulent business, while the joke makes him a racket-user on court.

clue.text: Crockery symbolised by RS (separately)

definitions.meaning: the communist nation whose emblems include the colour red and a star, though its stars are yellow

explanation.walkthrough: 'separately' is needed because the stars on China's flag are yellow on a red field.
explanation.definitionFit: China is porcelain crockery and also the country represented by red and by stars on its flag.

clue.text: RS gives insect to a god …

parts.note: an ant is an insect
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A star presents an ant to a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: RS means 'red star' throughout the puzzle; Antares is the red heart of Scorpius.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is a red supergiant star in the constellation Scorpius.

clue.text: Net-like arrangement of trailer with copper in it

indicators.note: with the metal symbol placed in it, inside the reordered letters
an arrangement of the word trailer means its letters are reordered

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A mesh-like pattern of the caravan with a police officer inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement of' gives RETILAR, and 'in it' sets the metal inside. 'copper' wants to be a policeman; it is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticular means forming a network, from Latin reticulum, a little net.

clue.text: … who damages RS (not technically)

definitions.meaning: the red planet, a red heavenly body loosely called a star though it is not one

explanation.walkthrough: 'who' follows on from the god Ares in 13: Mars is his Roman counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to spoil, and Mars is the red planet, a red 'star' only loosely.

clue.text: One taking taxi without cry of pain is ill at ease in society

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the passenger word surrounds the cry

parts.note: a fare is a passenger in a taxi
ouch is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A cab passenger who stifles a yelp is socially awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here keeps its old sense of outside, so the passenger word surrounds the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Farouche, borrowed from French, means shy and sullen, awkward in company.

clue.text: Original RS, given time, does bird

parts.note: RS in its original full form, not replaced by a synonym, is red star

explanation.surface: The first red star, with time, becomes a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' says the abbreviation RS is spelt out as RED STAR rather than turned into a star's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with a reddish tail.

clue.text: Return of stake with a hole in the crust

indicators.note: return of means the word for a stake is turned back to front

parts.note: an ante is a poker player's stake

explanation.surface: Getting your bet back along with a hole in the pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crust' suggests bread or pie; it is the Earth's crust, and a volcano is a hole in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a Sicilian volcano, a vent in the Earth's crust.

clue.text: An unprepossessing person in port

parts.note: taken as written
a twerp is a silly, unimpressive person

explanation.surface: A rather unattractive individual is found in a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major Belgian seaport.

clue.text: Piece of writing in bad French?

definitions.meaning: in French '...' means not good, i.e. naughty

explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a section of a written work, and 'pas sage' is French for not well behaved.

clue.text: Unknown king in front page with a fever

indicators.note: in places the unknown and king letters inside the front-page abbreviation

parts.note: pi is printers' term for the front pages of a book (preliminary pages, prelims)
y is a mathematical unknown
rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: An anonymous monarch, front-page news, is running a temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrexia is the medical term for fever.

clue.text: Medal in transport for slope in road

indicators.note: in puts the decoration inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a means of transport
MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: An award carried in a vehicle for the road's incline.
explanation.definitionFit: Camber is the convex curve of a road surface, letting water drain away.

clue.text: All set inside for sign of respiratory problem

indicators.note: inside places the word for set within the word for all

parts.note: sum means the total, all
put means set or placed

explanation.surface: Everything is placed indoors because of a chest complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputum is phlegm coughed up, a symptom of chest infections.

clue.text: Snake in charge of jelly

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A serpent supervising the jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock.

clue.text: Despotic Tony ran us ragged

indicators.note: ragged suggests something torn and disordered, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An autocratic Tony wore us out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrannous means ruling cruelly and oppressively, like a despot.

clue.text: Suitable post for the chronic hellraiser

indicators.note: the run of letters is found within the following words, standing for the post

explanation.surface: A fitting job for the habitual troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or position that suits someone well.

clue.text: Get ex-blue to reveal RS

indicators.note: to reveal implies the letters are reorganised to show something new

explanation.surface: A former Oxbridge sportsman exposes a star.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsperson. BETELGEUX is an old spelling of Betelgeuse, the red supergiant in Orion.
explanation.definitionFit: Betelgeux, an older spelling of Betelgeuse, is a red supergiant in Orion, a red star.

clue.text: Companies needing a hot drink

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company; companies gives two of them
the second company abbreviation

explanation.surface: Firms need a warming beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot drink made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: See 7
Cultured pearl to effect integration of substitute

indicators.note: cultured hints at something cultivated and reshaped, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: to cement is to bind things together, integrate them

explanation.surface: An artificial pearl used to bind things together stands in for the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A replacement is something or someone taking the place of another, a substitute.
